newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Barley Board boosts malt barley pool.
newsitem.headline: Australian Barley Board boosts malt barley pool.

text.p: The Australian Barley Board (ABB) raised its pool price for malting barley, left its price for feed barley steady and said world barley prices were poised to move.

The ABB raised its malting barley pool price by A$6 a tonne to A$198 a tonne for the states of South Australia and Victoria but held its feed estimate steady at A$153 a tonne for South Australia and A$160 for Victoria.
Australia would not have a large amount of malting barley for export this season, said the ABB, which markets barley from the states of South Australia and Victoria.
Recent rain firmed Australian crop prospects and harvests in Europe and Canada were getting under way, the ABB said.
"The world barley market is poised to move."
"We are entering the critical period when we start to see just how much barley really is going to be produced in the Northern Hemisphere," the ABB said.
Recent rain had firmed Australia's crop prospects slightly, but the season had a long way to go, it said.
"We don't believe world market prices have taken account yet of how critical the Australian situation still is, particularly (for) malting barley," it said.

"Around half the world trade in malting barley normally comes from Australia, and while at present we do expect to have some malting barley for export, the tonnage won't be large, hence our lift in malting pool forecast," the board said.
In contrast, the world feed grain market looked like being reasonably well supplied, particularly with corn from the United States, it said.
Prices in Victoria were presently very high but with a little more rain spring pasture growth in grazing areas would probably reduce demand somewhat, it said.
